extracted.intended_audience: journal publishers, editors, authors, reviewers, and readers
extracted.subtask_description: Define and standardize terminology for external peer review of journal articles so publishers and the community can more clearly describe, compare, and implement peer review practices (with potential future expansion to books, preprints, and data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard definitions for different peer review models
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides standard definitions for different peer review models to bring greater clarity and consistency in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formalized into an ANSI/NISO standard (July 2023). Intended to be adopted across publishers to enhance transparency and allow the community to assess and compare practices between journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key elements addressed by the terminology; relates to the transparency of identities in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies levels of identity disclosure or anonymity in review (e.g., who knows or sees whom). The terminology supports implementation options such as author choice around anonymity and helps stakeholders understand and report identity practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key elements; defines the nature and extent of interactions among reviewers and between reviewers and authors during the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to standardize whether and how reviewers communicate with each other or the authors (e.g., independent anonymous reports vs. interactive review) so practices are comparable across journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published review process information
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key elements; standardizes what information about the review process is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages consistent disclosure of review-process metadata (so journals can describe which model was used and enable comparison). The stated aim is to enhance clarity and consistency for authors, reviewers, editors, and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the four key elements; sets expectations for commenting on articles after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers whether post-publication comments are permitted, how they are managed/published, and how they relate to the formal review history, to ensure consistent practices and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: focus on external review of journal articles
rubrics_metrics.description: The terminology specifically focuses on the external review of journal articles, with potential future expansion to books, preprints, and data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Current applicability is to journal external peer review; the standard and its promoting committee plan wider implementation but note the initial scope is journal articles.
